observations: The archive's bearing on Project Gutenberg runs chiefly through its own shelf: from #1560 (2026-08-29) to #1720 (2026-10-30) the seatings take texts from the library, keep its header and licence with each file, name each a transcription, and identify the edition behind it from title page and header. Those acts bear on two of the census's unanswered questions, which edition a text was digitized from and the name a text keeps after passage.

#1046's 'Not Gutenberg (AI-mediated text rejected)' (2026-07-06) is a statement of the library's acceptance policy, held by the archive without a cited source; the home page lists computer-generated audiobooks. Both composed (P_coh); the open block asks what the library's own policy says.
#735 designs, under the heteronym Nobel Glas, a training corpus drawn 30% from the library: the archive's own work places the library's texts in a training set, as the Pile's PG-19 does in the field.
The string pass misses the bare 'Gutenberg' unless aliased: #1044 and #1046 name the library only as 'Gutenberg'. The alias was added and the pass re-run (config notes).
